slides.title: Consistent Hashing Overview
content: Consistent hashing is a data distribution technique that maps both keys and servers onto a circular hash space
It minimizes data movement when servers are added or removed
Used in distributed systems to handle dynamic scaling
Avoids large-scale rehashing compared to traditional hashing
Ensures efficient and scalable data distribution

slides.title: Why Consistent Hashing is Needed
content: Traditional hashing uses modulo which changes when number of servers changes
Server addition or removal causes massive data reshuffling
Distributed systems require dynamic scaling and fault tolerance
Consistent hashing reduces data movement to a small subset
Improves system stability during scaling operations

slides.title: Core Working Principle
content: Hash both server IDs and data keys into a hash space
Place them on a circular structure called a hash ring
Each key is assigned to the next server in clockwise direction
Supports wrap-around when reaching end of ring
Ensures minimal changes when system topology changes

slides.title: Hash Ring Concept
content: Hash ring is a circular representation of the hash space
Typical range is from 0 to 2 power 32 minus 1
Both servers and keys are placed on the ring
Lookup is performed using clockwise traversal
Eliminates dependency on total number of servers

slides.title: Virtual Nodes Concept
content: Virtual nodes are multiple logical representations of a single physical server
Each physical server is mapped to multiple points on the ring
Improves load balancing across servers
Prevents uneven distribution and hotspot issues
Supports heterogeneous server capacities

slides.title: Benefits of Virtual Nodes
content: Ensures uniform data distribution across servers
Reduces load imbalance and hotspots
Improves fault tolerance when nodes fail
Allows smooth scaling when adding or removing servers
Provides flexibility in handling different server capacities

slides.title: Adding a Server
content: Create multiple virtual nodes for the new server
Hash and insert them into the ring
Identify the previous node positions
Move only keys in the affected range to the new server
Other keys remain unchanged

slides.title: Removing a Server
content: Identify all virtual nodes of the server
Remove them from the hash ring
Reassign affected keys to the next clockwise server
Only a small portion of data is moved
No global redistribution is required

slides.title: Data Structures Used
content: Sorted map or tree-based structure is commonly used
Maintains order of nodes on the ring
Supports efficient insertion, deletion, and lookup
Allows quick clockwise search for key assignment
Time complexity for lookup is logarithmic

slides.title: Advantages of Consistent Hashing
content: Minimizes data movement during scaling
Provides high scalability and flexibility
Ensures high availability and fault tolerance
Supports smooth horizontal scaling
Avoids complete rehashing of data

slides.title: Disadvantages of Consistent Hashing
content: More complex than simple hashing methods
Requires additional memory for metadata
Load imbalance can occur without virtual nodes
Implementation requires sorted data structures
Needs careful handling in distributed systems

slides.title: Real-World Applications
content: Used in distributed caching systems like Redis and Memcached
Applied in load balancing mechanisms
Used in sharded databases for data distribution
Common in distributed storage systems
Used in large-scale web crawling systems

slides.title: Important Concepts
content: Hash function converts input into fixed-size numeric value
Hash space is the range of possible hash outputs
Clockwise lookup finds the next server for a key
Rebalancing refers to moving data after topology changes
Hotspot occurs when one server receives excessive traffic

slides.title: Scaling and Rebalancing
content: Consistent hashing supports horizontal scaling efficiently
Only nearby keys are affected during scaling operations
Reduces system downtime and data movement cost
Ensures stable performance under dynamic changes
Helps maintain system efficiency at large scale

slides.title: Final Summary
content: Consistent hashing distributes data across servers using a circular hash ring
It minimizes data movement when servers are added or removed
Virtual nodes improve load balancing and fault tolerance
Widely used in distributed systems for scalability
Provides efficient and reliable data distribution at scale
